$why: Moved out of spec-mode-runner.js on 2026-08-16. The labelled STORY block handed to the spec
agents, and the retrieved-documents notice that goes with it.
TWO BODIES, because the notice is a prompt in its own right and was nested inside one of the
outer block's interpolations. A first attempt mapped every ${...} to a placeholder and
produced a template that looked complete while that paragraph stayed in the script — it
passed a syntax check and a module load without complaint. A half-migration is the failure
this whole exercise exists to end.
description: The labelled story block handed to a spec agent, and its retrieved-documents notice.

bodies.block:
__PERSONA__STORY
Title: __TITLE__
Description: __DESCRIPTION__
Components: __COMPONENTS__
Declared files: __DECLARED_FILES__

LINKS FOUND IN THIS TICKET:
__LINK_BLOCK__

COMMENT THREAD (context for judging relevance — a link's surrounding discussion often says why it was posted):
__COMMENT_BLOCK__
__RETRIEVED_DOCS__
bodies.retrieved_docs:
ALREADY RETRIEVED — these documents have been fetched for you and written to disk. Read them
with read_file rather than fetching them again; the text is the same and it costs you nothing:
__DOC_PATHS__
A document listed here that you did not read is a document you cannot quote.

$mayBeEmptyWhy.__DOC_PATHS__: reviewTicketLinks defaults docPaths to [], and the caller passes ticketDocPaths which is empty whenever no document was fetched — including when retrieval FAILED, a path that logs "agents will have quotes only" and carries on. Undeclared, the renderer threw, the caller swallowed it in a try/catch, and the whole ticket-link review silently did not happen.
$mayBeEmptyWhy.__RETRIEVED_DOCS__: same condition: no documents retrieved is ordinary, not a failed lookup.
$mayBeEmptyWhy.__COMMENT_BLOCK__: a ticket with no comments is ordinary.
